newsitem.title: UK: British photo plane for Zaire lands in Uganda.
newsitem.headline: British photo plane for Zaire lands in Uganda.

text.p: A British photo-reconnaissance plane which is due to assess the refugee crisis in Zaire landed in Uganda on Thursday, the Ministry of Defence said.

The Canberra PR9 jet, along with a 50-man team and three giant Hercules transport aircraft, touched down at Entebbe near Lake Victoria, 20 miles (30 km) south of the Ugandan capital Kampala, a ministry spokesman said.
"Entebbe is close to the zone which we want to cover," an MOD spokesman told Reuters. "The Canberra may start taking pictures tomorrow -- it all depends on the weather."
The reconnaissance mission follows Britain's decision to put on hold its plans to send combat troops to eastern Zaire after news that up to 500,000 refugees had returned home to Rwanda.

Entebbe is around 320 miles (500 km) or less than an hour's flying time northeast of the eastern Zaire city of Bukavu, an area where hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees are thought to be massed on wooded hillsides.
The Hercules transports are equipped with mobile photographic cabins enabling the crew to process and enhance photographs in the field.

The government said on Wednesday Britain remained prepared to take part in a multinational military force in Zaire but along with other Western nations needed more information before it could decide on how to help refugees returning to Rwanda.

The government has said it may not be necessary to send combat troops now that many refugees had returned home but still thought humanitarian aid would be required to help ease of the plight of the estimated 700,000 refugees in the area.

The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Thursday it had located -- for the first time in weeks -- up to 700,000 missing Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire with Western satellite pictures and overflights.
The photo-reconnaissance team is expected to stay in the region for around a week, the ministry said.
The British move follows news on Tuesday the United States had scaled back its plans to send troops to Zaire. The U.S. said it would send less than 1,000 logistics personnel to aid Rwandan refugees.
